mainEntity.name: What is the digital asset question on Form 1040?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a mandatory question at the top of Form 1040 (and 1040-SR, 1040-NR, 1041, 1065, 1120, 1120-S, and a version on Form 709) asking whether the taxpayer received or disposed of a digital asset or a financial interest in a digital asset during the tax year. Every taxpayer must check Yes or No, under penalties of perjury.

mainEntity.name: Who has to answer the digital asset question?

acceptedAnswer.text: Everyone who files a covered return, whether or not they own or transacted in digital assets. A taxpayer with no digital asset activity checks No. The question is mandatory for all filers, not just those with digital asset transactions.

mainEntity.name: When should I check Yes on the digital asset question?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check Yes if you sold, exchanged, or otherwise disposed of a digital asset; received digital assets as payment, reward, award, or from mining, staking, or a hard-fork airdrop; paid for goods or services with digital assets; paid a transaction fee with digital assets; gifted or donated digital assets; disposed of a digital-asset ETF; or engaged in stablecoin transactions.

mainEntity.name: When can I check No on the digital asset question?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check No if you did not own any digital assets, only held digital assets in a wallet or account without transacting, purchased digital assets with U.S. or other real currency without selling, or transferred digital assets between wallets or accounts you own or control — provided you did not pay a transaction fee with digital assets.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I answer the digital asset question incorrectly?

acceptedAnswer.text: The return is signed under penalties of perjury, so a wrong answer is an affirmative misstatement. Inaccurate reporting can trigger accuracy-related penalties under IRC Section 6662 (20 percent for substantial valuation misstatements, 40 percent for gross), interest, civil fraud penalties in deliberate cases, and criminal referral in serious ones.

mainEntity.name: Do I need an appraisal to answer the digital asset question?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The checkbox itself requires no valuation. An appraisal becomes necessary when the activity behind a Yes answer creates a valuation obligation: gifts above the annual exclusion, charitable contributions over $5,000, estates requiring date-of-death value, lost-basis reconstruction, and audit defense against challenged figures.

mainEntity.name: How does the digital asset question relate to Form 1099-DA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Form 1099-DA is the broker information return reporting gross proceeds and basis for digital asset transactions. The digital asset question on the tax return must be consistent with the activity reported on Forms 1099-DA. Mismatches between the return and broker data can trigger CP2000 notices and examination.

mainEntity.name: Do gifts of crypto require a qualified appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always, but the valuation must be supportable. Gifts above the $19,000 annual exclusion require a Form 709 filing reporting the date-of-gift fair market value. For assets with thin markets, a qualified appraisal provides the defensible value and also documents the donor's basis for the recipient — important because a recipient without basis documentation is treated as having zero basis.
